films.title: The Last Tram
films.synopsis: The last tram of the night goes down a street where nobody gets off. A 4-minute short film about the hours when a city becomes quiet and empty.

scenes.speaker: Narrator
scenes.line: The last tram leaves the square at eleven forty.
scenes.translation: El último tranvía sale de la plaza a las once y cuarenta.

scenes.speaker: Narrator
scenes.line: By then the shops have closed and the square belongs to the people who have nowhere else to be.
scenes.translation: Para entonces las tiendas han cerrado y la plaza es de quienes no tienen otro sitio donde estar.

scenes.speaker: Old man
scenes.line: You are the last one?
scenes.translation: ¿Usted es el último?

scenes.speaker: Driver
scenes.line: I am the last one.
scenes.translation: Soy el último.

scenes.speaker: Old man
scenes.line: Then I will wait for you.
scenes.translation: Entonces lo espero a usted.

scenes.speaker: Narrator
scenes.line: He says it as if it were obvious. As if waiting for a tram at midnight were a thing that people did every night of their lives.
scenes.translation: Lo dice como si fuera obvio. Como si esperar un tranvía a medianoche fuera algo que la gente hiciera todas las noches de su vida.

scenes.speaker: Driver
scenes.line: You will be here when I come back.
scenes.translation: Usted estará aquí cuando yo vuelva.

scenes.speaker: Old man
scenes.line: I will be here when you come back.
scenes.translation: Estaré aquí cuando usted vuelva.

scenes.speaker: Narrator
scenes.line: The doors close. The tram takes the square, and the two of them watch each other through the glass.
scenes.translation: Las puertas se cierran. El tranvía cruza la plaza y los dos se miran a través del vidrio.

scenes.speaker: Narrator
scenes.line: The square is empty again. But something in it has changed, and nobody will say what.
scenes.translation: La plaza vuelve a estar vacía. Pero algo en ella ha cambiado, y nadie dirá qué.

comprehension.prompt: What time does the last tram leave?
comprehension.explanation: The narrator starts with "The last tram leaves the square at eleven forty."

comprehension.prompt: What does the old man say when the driver says he is the last one?
comprehension.explanation: The dialogue is: "You are the last one?" / "I am the last one." / "Then I will wait for you."

comprehension.prompt: What has changed at the end?

options.text: The square is empty, and nothing else.
The tram comes back with more passengers.
Something in the square has changed, but nobody can say what.

comprehension.explanation: «The square is empty again. But something in it has changed, and nobody will say what.»

films.title: Paper and Ink
films.synopsis: In a bookbinder's workshop, a man tries to write a letter he never sends. A short film about the gap between what we say and what we write.

scenes.speaker: Narrator
scenes.line: He has been coming to the workshop for eleven years. He brings the same book every time.
scenes.translation: Lleva once años viniendo al taller. Trae siempre el mismo libro.

scenes.speaker: Narrator
scenes.line: The book is called A Handbook of Correspondence. It was printed in nineteen fifty-four, and it is still, according to the owner, the only book about the subject that has ever been written.
scenes.translation: El libro se titula Manual de correspondencia. Se imprimió en mil novecientos cincuenta y cuatro y sigue siendo, según el dueño, el único libro sobre el tema que se ha escrito.

scenes.speaker: Binder
scenes.line: Ninety-one pages. Fifty-one of them are about envelopes.
scenes.translation: Noventa y una páginas. Cincuenta y una son sobre sobres.

scenes.speaker: Man
scenes.line: Envelopes are the difficult part. Paper is easy.
scenes.translation: Los sobres son la parte difícil. El papel es fácil.

scenes.speaker: Binder
scenes.line: You are not writing a letter. You are choosing a letter.
scenes.translation: Usted no está escribiendo una carta. Está eligiendo una carta.

scenes.speaker: Narrator
scenes.line: He says this without any weight. Then he looks at the book for a while, and corrects himself.
scenes.translation: Lo dice sin ninguna ironía. Luego mira el libro un rato y se corrige.

scenes.speaker: Man
scenes.line: You are not choosing a letter. You are choosing not to send one.
scenes.translation: Usted no está eligiendo una carta. Está eligiendo no enviar ninguna.

scenes.speaker: Narrator
scenes.line: The binder does not answer. She ties the pages, trims the edges, and sets the book on the shelf with the others, where it will wait.
scenes.translation: La encuadernadora no contesta. Ata las páginas, recorta los bordes y pone el libro en la estantería con los demás, donde esperará.

scenes.speaker: Narrator
scenes.line: He will be back on Thursday. He will bring the same book.
scenes.translation: Volverá el jueves. Traerá el mismo libro.

comprehension.prompt: How much of the handbook is about envelopes?
comprehension.explanation: "Ninety-one pages. Fifty-one of them are about envelopes." Fifty-one out of ninety-one is a little more than half.

comprehension.prompt: What does the man finally say he is choosing?
comprehension.explanation: «You are not choosing a letter. You are choosing not to send one.»

comprehension.prompt: What happens to the book at the end?

options.text: The bookbinder puts it on the shelf.
She gives it back without binding it.

comprehension.explanation: The bookbinder puts it on the shelf with the others, where it will wait.

films.title: Night Shift at the Observatory
films.synopsis: An astronomer alone in an observatory on a January night, talking to a radio that will never answer.

scenes.speaker: Narrator
scenes.line: The dome opens at sunset and closes at sunrise, and between those two events the observatory belongs to whoever is on shift.
scenes.translation: La cúpula se abre al atardecer y se cierra al amanecer, y entre esos dos hechos el observatorio pertenece a quien esté de turno.

scenes.speaker: Dr. Reyes
scenes.line: Meridian transit in forty minutes. Coffee number two is wrong, by the way. Somebody left the sugar out.
scenes.translation: Tránsito meridiano en cuarenta minutos. Por cierto, el café número dos está mal. Alguien dejó el azúcar fuera.

scenes.speaker: Narrator
scenes.line: Nobody answers. The radio on the desk is tuned to a frequency that stopped transmitting in nineteen ninety-eight, and she keeps it on because the static is easier to work with than silence.
scenes.translation: Nadie contesta. La radio del escritorio está sintonizada a una frecuencia que dejó de transmitir en mil novecientos noventa y ocho, y ella la deja encendida porque la estática es más fácil de trabajar que el silencio.

scenes.speaker: Dr. Reyes
scenes.line: Are you there?
scenes.translation: ¿Está ahí?

scenes.speaker: Narrator
scenes.line: The static does not answer either. But she asks again, and then again, because the question is not really for the radio.
scenes.translation: La estática tampoco contesta. Pero pregunta otra vez, y luego otra, porque la pregunta no es realmente para la radio.

scenes.speaker: Dr. Reyes
scenes.line: The plate is finished. One hundred and two exposures. It is the clearest night of the year so far, and there is nobody here to see it with.
scenes.translation: La placa está terminada. Ciento dos exposiciones. Es la noche más clara del año hasta ahora, y no hay nadie aquí para verlo con ella.

scenes.speaker: Narrator
scenes.line: She closes the dome at sunrise. It takes forty minutes and she does it alone, as she has done for six years.
scenes.translation: Cierra la cúpula al amanecer. Tarda cuarenta minutos y lo hace sola, como lleva haciendo seis años.

scenes.speaker: Dr. Reyes
scenes.line: Same frequency tomorrow?
scenes.translation: ¿Misma frecuencia mañana?

scenes.speaker: Narrator
scenes.line: The static keeps its shape. It is the only company that has never needed her to explain why she is still awake.
scenes.translation: La estática mantiene su forma. Es la única compañía que nunca ha necesitado que le explique por qué sigue despierta.

comprehension.prompt: Why does Dr. Reyes leave the radio on, even though nobody answers?

options.text: Because it works as an alarm clock.
Because the static is easier to work with than silence.
Because she is waiting for an urgent message.
Because she does not know how to turn it off.

comprehension.explanation: «The static is easier to work with than silence.»

comprehension.prompt: How many exposures does the plate have?
What does the narrator say about her question to the radio?

options.text: That the question is for the radio.
That the question is not really for the radio.
That the radio will finally answer.
That the question is an observatory rule.

comprehension.explanation: «The question is not really for the radio.»
